title: Which drives which? Directed cardiorespiratory coupling by Granger causality, checked against statsmodels

dataset.name: BIDMC PPG and Respiration Dataset
dataset.record: subject bidmc01, simultaneous RESP (respiration) + PLETH (PPG), decimated 125->25 Hz, 200 s segment (5001 samples); 20-subject summary over bidmc01-20
dataset.citation: Pimentel MAF et al. Toward a robust estimation of respiratory rate from pulse oximeters. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2017;64(8):1914-1923. BIDMC PPG and Respiration Dataset, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).

proposition: Coherence tells you two signals are coupled, but not which leads. Granger causality adds the ARROW: signal x Granger-causes y if x's past improves the prediction of y beyond y's own past. On a real simultaneous respiration + PPG recording, the ecosystem's grangerCausality measures the coupling in BOTH directions at once (Geweke's log-ratio of prediction-error variances) and finds it strong and bidirectional -- cardiorespiratory coupling runs both ways -- with respiration -> pulse the net-dominant direction (respiration modulating the peripheral pulse) in 15 of 20 BIDMC subjects. And the measure is trustworthy: grangerCausality reproduces the field-standard statsmodels.tsa.stattools.grangercausalitytests to ~3.5e-7 (an agreement, limited by statsmodels' intercept convention) and an independent from-scratch numpy OLS to ~1.8e-9 (the op's numerical floor), both directions, on the real signals -- and statsmodels' F-test confirms both directions are overwhelmingly significant (F ~ 54, p < 1e-100).

claims.statement: time-domain Granger causality respiration -> PPG pulse (Geweke log-variance-ratio) on BIDMC-01
time-domain Granger causality PPG pulse -> respiration on BIDMC-01
net Granger causality (respiration->pulse minus pulse->respiration) -- the directional asymmetry
max |grangerCausality - statsmodels grangercausalitytests| over both directions (agreement)
max |grangerCausality - independent numpy OLS| over both directions (op arithmetic, machine precision up to ridge)
BIDMC subjects (of 20) where respiration -> pulse is the net-dominant Granger direction

validation.reference: statsmodels.tsa.stattools.grangercausalitytests (Seabold & Perktold 2010) is the field-standard Granger-causality test; it fits the same restricted (target on its own lags) and unrestricted (target + driver lags) OLS regressions. With matched model order and demeaned signals, grangerCausality's Geweke log-variance-ratio reproduces statsmodels' (from its restricted/unrestricted SSRs) to max |diff| ~ 3.5e-7 -- an AGREEMENT, since statsmodels forces an intercept while the op demeans then fits without one. Against an independent from-scratch numpy OLS built to the op's exact construction, the agreement is ~1.8e-9 (the op's ridge-regularization floor), so the op's arithmetic is machine-precise. statsmodels' ssr_ftest confirms both directions are overwhelmingly significant (F ~ 54, p < 1e-100). The finding: cardiorespiratory coupling is bidirectional, with respiration -> pulse net-dominant in 15/20 BIDMC subjects.
validation.data: REAL -- BIDMC PPG and Respiration Dataset (PhysioNet), subject bidmc01 (machine validation) + bidmc01-20 (net-direction summary), RESP + PLETH decimated to 25 Hz
validation.note: The reproducible findings are (1) grangerCausality reproduces statsmodels' Granger regression to ~3.5e-7 and an independent numpy OLS to ~1.8e-9 on real BIDMC resp/PPG, both directions; (2) cardiorespiratory coupling is strong and bidirectional (both directions F ~ 54, p < 1e-100), with respiration -> pulse net-dominant in 15/20 subjects (mean net +0.032). HONEST scope: (1) the statsmodels agreement (~3.5e-7) is an AGREEMENT, NOT a machine-precision match -- statsmodels forces an intercept while the op demeans then fits without one, a convention difference on the order of the lag columns' edge-sample means; the op's OWN arithmetic is validated to ~1.8e-9 against an independent from-scratch numpy OLS (the op's 1e-8-relative ridge-regularization floor); (2) both directions are strongly significant -- cardiorespiratory coupling IS bidirectional (respiratory sinus arrhythmia AND cardioventilatory coupling), so the contribution is a VALIDATED directed-connectivity op plus a modest, honestly-reported net direction, NOT a claim of unidirectional causation; (3) Granger causality is PREDICTIVE (temporal-precedence) coupling, not proof of a physical causal mechanism; (4) time-domain parametric GC at a fixed model order (10 lags at 25 Hz); the net direction is subject-dependent (5/20 subjects show pulse -> respiration net-dominant); (5) single subject for the machine validation, 200 s segment; run_simulation = FALSE (deterministic OLS both sides).

open_questions.q: grangerCausality also implements a NONPARAMETRIC spectral path (Wilson minimum-phase factorization of the cross-spectrum, method='nonparametric'), giving frequency-resolved Granger causality -- which would show WHERE in the spectrum (the respiratory band vs the cardiac band) each direction dominates, and a conditional/multivariate GC would separate direct from mediated coupling. Extending this time-domain validation to the spectral and conditional cases -- and to a respiration -> instantaneous-heart-rate (RSA) tachogram design where the direction is textbook -- would turn a validated pairwise op into a network-physiology study. Documented, not escalated.
